sanskrit: yajño dānam adhyayanaṃ tapaś ca; catvāry etāny anvavetāni sadbhiḥ damaḥ satyam ārjavam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ; catvāry etāny anvavayanti santaḥ
english: Sacrifice, charity, study, and austerity — these four are ever attended by the good. Self-restraint, truth, straightforwardness, and non-cruelty — these four ever follow the righteous.

sanskrit: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā; na te vṛddhā ye na vadanti dharmam nāsau dharmo yatra na satyam asti; na tat satyaṃ yac chalenānuviddham
english: That is no assembly where there are no elders; those are no elders who do not speak of righteousness; that is no righteousness where there is no truth; that is no truth which is riddled with deceit.

sanskrit: satyaṃ rūpaṃ śrutaṃ vidyā kaulyaṃ śīlaṃ balaṃ dhanam śauryaṃ ca citrabhāṣyaṃ ca daśa saṃsargayonayaḥ
english: Truth, beauty, learning, knowledge, noble birth, good conduct, strength, wealth, valor, and eloquent speech — these ten are the sources of social association.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kurvan pāpakīrtiḥ pāpam evāśnute phalam puṇyaṃ kurvan puṇyakīrtiḥ puṇyam evāśnute phalam
english: One who does evil, renowned for evil, reaps only evil as fruit. One who does good, renowned for good, reaps only good as fruit.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ prajñāṃ nāśayati kriyamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ naṣṭaprajñaḥ pāpam eva nityam ārabhate naraḥ
english: Sin, committed again and again, destroys wisdom. The man whose wisdom is destroyed ever undertakes only sin.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ prajñāṃ vardhayati kriyamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ vṛddhaprajñaḥ puṇyam eva nityam ārabhate naraḥ
english: Virtue, practiced again and again, increases wisdom. The man whose wisdom has grown ever undertakes only virtue.

sanskrit: asūyako dandaśūko niṣṭhuro vairakṛn naraḥ sa kṛcchraṃ mahad āpnoti nacirāt pāpam ācaran
english: A man who is envious, venomous, cruel, and given to enmity meets with great distress before long, by his sinful conduct.

sanskrit: anasūyaḥ kṛtaprajñaḥ śobhanāny ācaran sadā akṛcchrāt sukham āpnoti sarvatra ca virājate
english: One who is free from envy, possessed of wisdom, and ever practicing noble deeds attains happiness without difficulty and shines forth everywhere.

sanskrit: prajñām evāgamayati yaḥ prājñebhyaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ prājño hy avāpya dharmārthau śaknoti sukham edhitum
english: He is truly learned who acquires wisdom from the wise. Indeed, a wise man, having attained righteousness and wealth, is able to prosper in happiness.

sanskrit: divasenaiva tat kuryād yena rātrau sukhaṃ vaset aṣṭamāsena tat kuryād yena varṣāḥ sukhaṃ vaset
english: In a single day one should do that by which one may dwell in comfort at night; in eight months one should do that by which one may dwell in comfort during the rains.

sanskrit: pūrve vayasi tat kuryād yena vṛddhaḥ sukhaṃ vaset yāvajjīvena tat kuryād yena pretya sukhaṃ vaset
english: In one's earlier years one should do that by which one may dwell in comfort when old; throughout one's life one should do that by which one may dwell in comfort after death.

sanskrit: jīrṇam annaṃ praśaṃsanti bhāryāṃ ca gatayauvanām śūraṃ vigatasaṃgrāmaṃ gatapāraṃ tapasvinam
english: People praise food only after it has been digested, a wife only after her youth has passed, a warrior only after the battle is over, and an ascetic only after he has crossed to the other shore.

sanskrit: dhanenādharmalabdhena yac chidram apidhīyate asaṃvṛtaṃ tad bhavati tato 'nyad avadīryate
english: When a gap is stopped up with wealth gained by unrighteousness, that gap remains uncovered, and from there another crack opens up.

sanskrit: gurur ātmavatāṃ śāstā śāstā rājā durātmanām atha pracchannapāpānāṃ śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ
english: A preceptor is the chastiser of those who are self-controlled; a king is the chastiser of the wicked; but Yama, the son of Vivasvat, is the chastiser of those who commit secret sins.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca kulānāṃ ca mahātmanām prabhavo nādhigantavyaḥ strīṇāṃ duścaritasya ca
english: The origin of sages, rivers, great-souled lineages, women, and of evil conduct — these should not be probed.

sanskrit: dvijātipūjābhirato dātā jñātiṣu cārjavī kṣatriyaḥ svargabhāg rājaṃś ciraṃ pālayate mahīm
english: A Kshatriya who delights in honoring the twice-born, who is generous, and who is straightforward toward his kinsmen shares in heaven and guards the earth for a long time, O king.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīṃ cinvanti puruṣās trayaḥ śūraś ca kṛtavidyaś ca yaś ca jānāti sevitum
english: Three kinds of men gather the golden flowers of the earth: the brave, the learned, and one who knows how to serve.

sanskrit: buddhiśreṣṭhāni karmāṇi bāhumadhyāni bhārata tāni jaṅghājaghanyāni bhārapratyavarāṇi ca
english: Deeds of intellect are the highest, O Bharata; deeds of the arms are middling; those of the legs are the lowest, being akin to burden-bearing.

sanskrit: duryodhane ca śakunau mūḍhe duḥśāsane tathā karṇe caiśvaryam ādhāya kathaṃ tvaṃ bhūtim icchasi
english: Having placed sovereignty in the foolish Duryodhana, Shakuni, Duhshasana, and Karna, how do you seek prosperity?

sanskrit: sarvair guṇair upetāś ca pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha pitṛvat tvayi vartante teṣu vartasva putravat
english: The Pandavas, O bull of the Bharatas, are endowed with every virtue and conduct themselves toward you as toward a father; conduct yourself toward them as toward sons.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ātreyasya ca saṃvādaṃ sādhyānāṃ ceti naḥ śrutam
english: Vidura said: On this point they cite this ancient legend — the dialogue between Atreya and the Sadhyas, as we have heard it.

sanskrit: carantaṃ haṃsarūpeṇa maharṣiṃ saṃśitavratam sādhyā devā mahāprājñaṃ paryapṛcchanta vai purā
english: In ancient times the Sadhya gods questioned the great sage of sharpened vows as he wandered in the form of a goose — that great knower of wisdom.

sanskrit: sādhyā devā vayam asmo maharṣe; dṛṣṭvā bhavantaṃ na śaknumo 'numātum śrutena dhīro buddhimāṃs tvaṃ mato naḥ; kāvyāṃ vācaṃ vaktum arhasy udārām
english: The Sadhya gods said: We are the Sadhyas, O great sage. Having seen you, we cannot form a full estimate of you. In our view you are wise and intelligent through your learning; you deserve to speak a noble and inspired word.

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca etat kāryam amarāḥ saṃśrutaṃ me; dhṛtiḥ śamaḥ satyadharmānuvṛttiḥ granthiṃ vinīya hṛdayasya sarvaṃ; priyāpriye cātmavaśaṃ nayīta
english: The goose said: This is the duty I have ever upheld, O immortals — steadiness, tranquility, adherence to truth and righteousness. Having loosened every knot of the heart, bring the pleasant and the unpleasant under your own control.

sanskrit: ākruśyamāno nākrośen manyur eva titikṣitaḥ ākroṣṭāraṃ nirdahati sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati
english: When reviled one should not revile in return; anger that is endured burns up the reviler and gathers his good deeds.

sanskrit: nākrośī syān nāvamānī parasya; mitradrohī nota nīcopasevī na cātimānī na ca hīnavṛtto; rūkṣāṃ vācaṃ ruśatīṃ varjayīta
english: One should not be abusive, nor contemptuous of others, nor a betrayer of friends, nor a frequenter of the low; one should not be arrogant, nor of base conduct; one should avoid harsh and wounding speech.

sanskrit: marmāṇy asthīni hṛdayaṃ tathāsūn; ghorā vāco nirdahantīha puṃsām tasmād vācaṃ ruśatīṃ rūkṣarūpāṃ; dharmārāmo nityaśo varjayīta
english: Terrible words burn up the vital points, bones, heart, and very life-breaths of men here. Therefore one who delights in righteousness should ever avoid speech that is wounding and harsh in nature.

sanskrit: aruṃtudaṃ paruṣaṃ rūkṣavācaṃ; vākkaṇṭakair vitudantaṃ manuṣyān vidyād alakṣmīkatamaṃ janānāṃ; mukhe nibaddhāṃ nirṛtiṃ vahantam
english: One who pierces the vital spots, is harsh, speaks rough words, and stings people with thorns of speech — know him as the most miserable of men, carrying ruin bound upon his face.

sanskrit: paraś ced enam adhividhyeta bāṇair; bhṛśaṃ sutīkṣṇair analārkadīptaiḥ viricyamāno 'py atiricyamāno; vidyāt kaviḥ sukṛtaṃ me dadhāti
english: If another pierces him deeply with arrows blazing like fire and sun, the wise man, though diminished, knows while gaining even more: 'He is piling up merit for me.'

sanskrit: yadi santaṃ sevate yady asantaṃ; tapasvinaṃ yadi vā stenam eva vāso yathā raṅgavaśaṃ prayāti; tathā sa teṣāṃ vaśam abhyupaiti
english: Whether one serves the good, the wicked, an ascetic, or even a thief, just as a garment takes on the color of its dye, so one comes under their influence.

sanskrit: vādaṃ tu yo na pravaden na vādayed; yo nāhataḥ pratihanyān na ghātayet yo hantukāmasya na pāpam icchet; tasmai devāḥ spṛhayanty āgatāya
english: He who does not begin a quarrel nor incite others to quarrel, who does not strike back when unstruck nor slay, who does not desire the sin of one who wishes to kill him — to such a one the gods aspire when he arrives.

sanskrit: avyāhṛtaṃ vyāhṛtāc chreya āhuḥ; satyaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tad dvitīyam priyaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tat tṛtīyaṃ; dharmyaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tac caturtham
english: They say silence is better than speech. If one must speak, let what is said be true — that is second. Let what is said be pleasant — that is third. Let what is said be righteous — that is fourth.

sanskrit: yādṛśaiḥ saṃvivadate yādṛśāṃś copasevate yādṛg icchec ca bhavituṃ tādṛg bhavati pūruṣaḥ
english: With whomever a man associates in argument, whomever he serves, and whatever he wishes to become — such does a man become.

sanskrit: yato yato nivartate tatas tato vimucyate nivartanād dhi sarvato na vetti duḥkham aṇv api
english: From whatever a man turns away, from that he is released. By turning away from everything he does not know even a particle of suffering.

sanskrit: na jīyate nota jigīṣate 'nyān; na vairakṛc cāpratighātakaś ca nindāpraśaṃsāsu samasvabhāvo; na śocate hṛṣyati naiva cāyam
english: He is neither defeated nor seeks to defeat others; he makes no enemies and retaliates against none; his nature is equal in blame and praise alike; he neither grieves nor rejoices.

sanskrit: bhāvam icchati sarvasya nābhāve kurute matim satyavādī mṛdur dānto yaḥ sa uttamapūruṣaḥ
english: He who wishes the well-being of all, whose mind is not set on harm, who speaks truth, is gentle and self-controlled — that one is a highest person.

sanskrit: nānarthakaṃ sāntvayati pratijñāya dadāti ca rāddhāparāddhe jānāti yaḥ sa madhyamapūruṣaḥ
english: He who does not soothe with empty words, who gives what he has promised, and who understands success and failure — that one is a middling person.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tūpahantā na śāstā; nāvartate manyuvaśāt kṛtaghnaḥ na kasya cin mitram atho durātmā; kalāś caitā adhamasyeha puṃsaḥ
english: One who is a vexer and not a chastiser, who does not turn back from the grip of anger, who is ungrateful, no one's friend, and of wicked soul — these are the qualities of the lowest man in this world.

sanskrit: na śraddadhāti kalyāṇaṃ parebhyo 'py ātmaśaṅkitaḥ nirākaroti mitrāṇi yo vai so 'dhamapūruṣaḥ
english: He who does not trust in good even from others, who is suspicious even of himself, and who rejects his friends — he indeed is the lowest person.

sanskrit: uttamān eva seveta prāpte kāle tu madhyamān adhamāṃs tu na seveta ya icchec chreya ātmanaḥ
english: One who wishes his own good should serve only the best; in due time also the middling; but should never serve the lowest.

sanskrit: prāpnoti vai vittam asadbalena; nityotthānāt prajñayā pauruṣeṇa na tv eva samyag labhate praśaṃsāṃ; na vṛttam āpnoti mahākulānām
english: One gains wealth by the strength of the wicked, through constant rising, through wisdom and manliness; yet such a one does not rightly earn praise, nor does one acquire the conduct of great families.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca mahākulānāṃ spṛhayanti devā; dharmārthavṛddhāś ca bahuśrutāś ca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vidura praśnam etaṃ; bhavanti vai kāni mahākulāni
english: Dhritarashtra said: The gods desire great families, as do those grown in righteousness and wealth, and the greatly learned. I ask you this question, Vidura: what indeed are great families?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca tapo damo brahmavit tvaṃ vitānāḥ; puṇyā vivāhāḥ satatānnadānam yeṣv evaite sapta guṇā bhavanti; samyag vṛttās tāni mahākulāni
english: Vidura said: Austerity, self-restraint, knowledge of Brahman, spreading of learning, auspicious marriages, constant gift of food — in those families where these seven qualities prevail and righteous conduct is well-practiced, those are great families.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ na vṛttaṃ vyathate na yonir; vṛttaprasādena caranti dharmam ye kīrtim icchanti kule viśiṣṭāṃ; tyaktānṛtās tāni mahākulāni
english: Those whose conduct does not waver and whose lineage is unshaken, who walk in righteousness through the grace of their conduct, who desire distinguished fame within the family, and who have abandoned untruth — those are great families.

sanskrit: anijyayāvivāhaiś ca vedasyotsādanena ca kulāny akulatāṃ yānti dharmasyātikrameṇa ca
english: By absence of sacrifice, by improper marriages, by the suppression of the Vedas, and by transgression of righteousness, families fall into the state of non-families.

sanskrit: devadravyavināśena brahmasvaharaṇena ca kulāny akulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca
english: By destruction of the property of gods, by seizure of priestly wealth, and by transgression against Brahmins, families fall into the state of non-families.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavāt parivādāc ca bhārata kulāny akulatāṃ yānti nyāsāpaharaṇena ca
english: By disrespect toward Brahmins, by slander of them, O Bharata, and by misappropriation of deposits entrusted to one's care, families fall into the state of non-families.

sanskrit: kulāni samupetāni gobhiḥ puruṣato 'śvataḥ kulasaṃkhyāṃ na gacchanti yāni hīnāni vṛttataḥ
english: Families well endowed with cattle, men, and horses do not attain the rank of great families if they are deficient in right conduct.

sanskrit: vṛttatas tv avihīnāni kulāny alpadhanāny api kulasaṃkhyāṃ tu gacchanti karṣanti ca mahad yaśaḥ
english: But families that are not deficient in conduct, even if they are of small wealth, do attain the rank of great families and draw great glory to themselves.

sanskrit: mā naḥ kule vairakṛt kaś cid astu; rājāmātyo mā parasvāpahārī mitradrohī naikṛtiko 'nṛtī vā; pūrvāśī vā pitṛdevātithibhyaḥ
english: Let there be no enemy-maker in our family; let there be no minister of a king who seizes others' property; no betrayer of friends, no deceitful one, no speaker of falsehood, no one who eats before the ancestors, gods, and guests.

sanskrit: yaś ca no brāhmaṇaṃ hanyād yaś ca no brāhmaṇān dviṣet na naḥ sa samitiṃ gacched yaś ca no nirvapet kṛṣim
english: Let the one who would kill our Brahmin, the one who would hate our Brahmins, and the one who would render our farming useless — let none such enter our assembly.

sanskrit: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā satām etāni geheṣu nocchidyante kadā cana
english: Grass, ground, water, and as a fourth — kindly and true speech: these in the houses of the good are never absent at any time.

sanskrit: śraddhayā parayā rājann upanītāni satkṛtim pravṛttāni mahāprājña dharmiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: O king, these are offered with the highest faith, properly honored, practiced among the righteous of great wisdom and meritorious deeds, O greatly wise one.

sanskrit: sūkṣmo 'pi bhāraṃ nṛpate syandano vai; śakto voḍhuṃ na tathānye mahījāḥ evaṃ yuktā bhārasahā bhavanti; mahākulīnā na tathānye manuṣyāḥ
english: Even a slender chariot, O king, is able to bear a load, while other earthly things cannot bear it in the same way. In the same way those endowed with noble birth are able to bear burdens, while other men cannot bear them similarly.

sanskrit: na tan mitraṃ yasya kopād bibheti; yad vā mitraṃ śaṅkitenopacaryam yasmin mitre pitarīvāśvasīta; tad vai mitraṃ saṃgatānītarāṇi
english: That is no friend whom one fears because of anger; nor is that a friend who must be approached with suspicion. The friend in whom one can take confidence as in a father — that indeed is a friend; others are merely associates.

sanskrit: yadi ced apy asaṃbandho mitrabhāvena vartate sa eva bandhus tan mitraṃ sā gatis tatparāyaṇam
english: If even an unrelated person conducts himself with the spirit of friendship, he alone is a kinsman, that is a friend, that is a refuge, that is one's ultimate resort.

sanskrit: calacittasya vai puṃso vṛddhān anupasevataḥ pāriplavamater nityam adhruvo mitrasaṃgrahaḥ
english: For a man of unsteady mind who does not serve the elders, whose understanding is ever wavering, the acquisition of friends is always insecure.

sanskrit: calacittam anātmānam indriyāṇāṃ vaśānugam arthāḥ samativartante haṃsāḥ śuṣkaṃ saro yathā
english: Riches pass beyond a man of unsteady mind, lacking self-mastery, who follows the lead of his senses — just as geese pass beyond a dried-up lake.

sanskrit: akasmād eva kupyanti prasīdanty animittataḥ śīlam etad asādhūnām abhraṃ pāriplavaṃ yathā
english: They grow angry without cause and become pleased without reason — this is the character of the wicked, like a drifting cloud.

sanskrit: satkṛtāś ca kṛtārthāś ca mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye tān mṛtān api kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnān nopabhuñjate
english: Those who, when honored and when their purposes are served, do not become friends — even flesh-eaters, when they are dead, do not consume such ungrateful ones.

sanskrit: arthayed eva mitrāṇi sati vāsati vā dhane nānarthayan vijānāti mitrāṇāṃ sāraphalgutām
english: One should petition one's friends whether there is wealth or not; one who does not petition does not come to know the soundness or shallowness of friends.

sanskrit: saṃtāpād bhraśyate rūpaṃ saṃtāpād bhraśyate balam saṃtāpād bhraśyate jñānaṃ saṃtāpād vyādhim ṛcchati
english: Through anguish beauty fades, through anguish strength fades, through anguish knowledge fades, through anguish one falls into disease.

sanskrit: anavāpyaṃ ca śokena śarīraṃ copatapyate amitrāś ca prahṛṣyanti mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Nothing is attained through grief, and the body is afflicted; enemies rejoice. Therefore do not set your mind on grief.

sanskrit: punar naro mriyate jāyate ca; punar naro hīyate vardhate punaḥ punar naro yācati yācyate ca; punar naraḥ śocate śocyate punaḥ
english: Again a man dies and is born; again a man declines and rises again; again a man begs and is begged of; again a man grieves and is grieved over.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavau ca; lābhālābhau maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca paryāyaśaḥ sarvam iha spṛśanti; tasmād dhīro naiva hṛṣyen na śocet
english: Happiness and suffering, existence and non-existence, gain and loss, death and life — all these touch everything here in turn. Therefore the wise man should neither rejoice nor grieve.

sanskrit: calāni hīmāni ṣaḍindriyāṇi; teṣāṃ yad yad vartate yatra yatra tatas tataḥ sravate buddhir asya; chidrodakumbhād iva nityam ambhaḥ
english: These six senses are unstable and restless; wherever and toward whatever each of them moves, from there and there flows away his understanding — like water ever flowing from a cracked pot.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tanur ucchaḥ śikhī rājā mithyopacarito mayā mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ yuddhenāntaṃ kariṣyati
english: Dhritarashtra said: The slender, lofty, crested king Yudhishthira has been wrongly treated by me; he will bring the end of my dull-witted sons through battle.

sanskrit: nityodvignam idaṃ sarvaṃ nityodvignam idaṃ manaḥ yat tat padam anudvignaṃ tan me vada mahāmate
english: All this is ever agitated, this mind is ever agitated; tell me, O greatly wise one, of that state which is free from agitation.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca nānyatra vidyātapasor nānyatrendriyanigrahāt nānyatra lobhasaṃtyāgāc chāntiṃ paśyāmi te 'nagha
english: Vidura said: I see peace for you nowhere other than in knowledge and austerity, nowhere other than in the restraint of the senses, nowhere other than in the abandonment of greed, O sinless one.

sanskrit: buddhyā bhayaṃ praṇudati tapasā vindate mahat guruśuśrūṣayā jñānaṃ śāntiṃ tyāgena vindati
english: Through wisdom one drives away fear; through austerity one attains greatness; through service to elders one attains knowledge; through renunciation one attains peace.

sanskrit: anāśritā dānapuṇyaṃ vedapuṇyam anāśritāḥ rāgadveṣavinirmuktā vicarantīha mokṣiṇaḥ
english: Unattached to the merit of giving, unattached to the merit of Vedic learning, freed from passion and hatred — those seeking liberation wander here.

sanskrit: svadhītasya suyuddhasya sukṛtasya ca karmaṇaḥ tapasaś ca sutaptasya tasyānte sukham edhate
english: At the end of that which is well studied, well fought, well done as a deed, and austerity well practiced — happiness flourishes.

sanskrit: svāstīrṇāni śayanāni prapannā; na vai bhinnā jātu nidrāṃ labhante na strīṣu rājan ratim āpnuvanti; na māgadhaiḥ stūyamānā na sūtaiḥ
english: Even when they have attained well-spread couches, the disunited never truly obtain sleep; they do not find pleasure in women, O king, nor when praised by bards and panegyrists.

sanskrit: na vai bhinnā jātu caranti dharmaṃ; na vai sukhaṃ prāpnuvantīha bhinnāḥ na vai bhinnā gauravaṃ mānayanti; na vai bhinnāḥ praśamaṃ rocayanti
english: The disunited never truly walk in righteousness; the disunited never truly attain happiness here; the disunited never truly honor dignity; the disunited never truly love peace.

sanskrit: na vai teṣāṃ svadate pathyam uktaṃ; yogakṣemaṃ kalpate nota teṣām bhinnānāṃ vai manujendra parāyaṇaṃ; na vidyate kiṃ cid anyad vināśāt
english: Beneficial counsel does not taste sweet to them; security and prosperity are not arranged for them; for the disunited, O lord of men, there is no resort whatsoever other than ruin.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvyaṃ goṣu saṃpannaṃ saṃbhāvyaṃ brāhmaṇe tapaḥ saṃbhāvyaṃ strīṣu cāpalyaṃ saṃbhāvyaṃ jñātito bhayam
english: Abundance is to be expected from cattle, austerity from a Brahmin, inconstancy from women, and danger from one's own kinsmen.

sanskrit: tantavo 'py āyatā nityaṃ tantavo bahulāś ca te bahūn bahutvād āyāsān sahantīty upamā satām
english: Threads, though individually slender and always extended, when they are many, because of their multitude bear many hardships — this is the simile of the righteous.

sanskrit: dhūmāyante vyapetāni jvalanti sahitāni ca dhṛtarāṣṭrolmukānīva jñātayo bharatarṣabha
english: Kindred separated from one another smolder and die out; united they blaze — like firebrands, O Dhritarashtra, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca ye śūrāḥ strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca vṛntād iva phalaṃ pakvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra patanti te
english: Those who are violent toward Brahmins, women, kinsmen, and cattle — they fall, O Dhritarashtra, like a ripe fruit from its stalk.

sanskrit: mahān apy ekajo vṛkṣo balavān supratiṣṭhitaḥ prasahya eva vātena śākhāskandhaṃ vimarditam
english: Even a great tree that stands alone, mighty and well-rooted, has its branches and trunk crushed outright by the wind.
